bounded_slice: Source-pin exact rmcp-v3.1.4 tasks/update wire/dispatch semantics and define one application-owned durable InputResponses transition validator with generation/CAS and a durable redrive-outbox boundary; stop before executor/effect work.

findings.update_task_wire: UpdateTaskParams contains task_id plus InputResponses. Exact release docs say every supplied response key MUST correspond to a currently-outstanding inputRequests key.
findings.task_state_wire: TaskPayload::InputRequired carries InputRequests; exact release docs describe those keys as arbitrary server-assigned identifiers unique over the task lifetime. tasks/update success returns TaskAckResult only; changed task state is observed through a later tasks/get.
findings.dispatch_boundary: Server dispatch validates the Tasks capability before ServerHandler::update_task and maps handler success to a task acknowledgement. The handler hook is therefore the application seam for durable response-transition validation before redrive.
findings.subset_inference: Pinned source requires every supplied key to be currently outstanding but does not require one update to answer all outstanding keys. Accepting a nonempty supplied key set as a subset is an application-owned strict interpretation, not an additional rmcp guarantee.
findings.opaque_values: InputResponses values are opaque JSON at this generic task layer. This validator checks task/status/key/generation invariants only; request-specific response-shape validation remains unresolved.
findings.durable_transition_rule: Load by task_id; require generation CAS match and status=input_required; reject an empty response map as an application no-op guard; require every supplied key to exist in current outstanding InputRequests; stage the whole change atomically; move accepted keys from outstanding into an accumulated accepted-response record; increment generation once. If outstanding keys remain, persist input_required with the reduced set. If none remain, persist working plus the accumulated responses and atomically append a redrive-outbox row bound to the new generation. Only after commit may a runtime redriver claim that generation.
findings.duplicate_rule: A committed response key is removed from outstanding, so replay of that key is rejected instead of reapplied. Concurrent same-generation writers are serialized by CAS: at most one commits and later writers must reread current state.
findings.crash_boundary: The final-response transaction must include the redrive outbox atomically with generation/status update. This removes commit-before-volatile-schedule orphaning for this transition slice; it does not make downstream external effects exactly-once.
findings.compiler_surface: No Rust compiler/runtime execution was performed in this slice; Rust compile success is not claimed.

application_owned_candidate: StoredInputRoundV1 holds round_id, outstanding InputRequests and accepted InputResponses. apply_input_responses(row, expected_generation, UpdateTaskParams) requires CAS generation equality, input_required state, nonempty responses, and keys subset of outstanding; stages changes on copies; moves accepted keys; bumps generation once; persists reduced input_required state or, when empty, working state plus an atomic redrive-outbox row for the new generation. Runtime redrive begins only after commit. Persistent-store code is NOT COMPILED.
